1. Governance, risk and accountability
Governance, risk appetite, ownership and oversight

NDIA must manage ICT disaster recovery as an enterprise governance, risk and internal-control capability with approved authority, defined risk appetite and tolerances, named business and ICT owners, measurable risk reporting, and architecture, change and investment gates that prevent systems entering operation without appropriate recoverability.

The NDIA must govern ICT disaster recovery as an enterprise risk control. Business and ICT owners must be named, recovery risk appetite and tolerances must be approved, recovery risks must be reported, and new or changed systems must not go live unless they can be recovered to agreed targets.
Governance and risk management
Critical

2. Scope, critical services and recovery objectives
Critical services, BIA, RTO/RPO and service continuity scope

NDIA must identify the services, systems, data, legacy platforms, suppliers and interdependencies that support NDIS outcomes, assess business and user impact, and set approved recovery priorities, maximum tolerable outages, recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives that align with business continuity and participant service needs.

The NDIA must identify which services, systems, data, suppliers and dependencies are critical to NDIS outcomes. Each critical service must have an approved business impact assessment, recovery priority, maximum tolerable outage, recovery time objective and recovery point objective aligned with business continuity and participant service needs.

3. Resilient architecture, cloud, hosting and dependencies
Architecture resilience, cloud/hosting assurance and physical dependencies

NDIA must design and operate production, backup, replication and recovery environments using resilient architecture, approved network and access controls, current asset and dependency records, certified or otherwise approved cloud, hosting and data-centre services, documented data locations, and physical protections proportionate to business impact and information sensitivity.

The NDIA must design and operate production and recovery environments so critical services can continue or be restored. Recovery architecture must use approved cloud, hosting, network and access controls, current asset and dependency records, known data locations and appropriate physical protection.

4. Backup, restoration and data integrity
Backups, restoration, immutable recovery and transaction integrity

NDIA must maintain protected and tested backups of important data, software, configurations and records, with retention aligned to approved RPO/RTO, recovery procedures that verify integrity and completeness, and additional reconciliation controls before restoring financial, claims, payment or other high-impact services.

The NDIA must keep recoverable backups of important data, software, configurations and records. Backups must be protected from unauthorised change or deletion, tested regularly, retained to meet approved recovery targets, and restored only after integrity and transaction checks are complete.

5. Cyber-resilient recovery controls
Baseline cyber controls for recovery readiness

NDIA must protect recovery capabilities with risk-based ISM, Essential Eight and ACSC cyber controls, including patching, hardening, application control, MFA, least-privilege and monitored administrative access, protected identity recovery, and heightened post-recovery monitoring before restored services are returned to normal operation.

The NDIA must protect recovery systems with cyber controls that match the risk. Recovery environments must use Essential Eight and ISM-aligned controls, including patching, hardening, application control, MFA, least privilege, protected administrator access, identity recovery and monitoring before services return to normal use.

6. Incident, ransomware and breach response integration
DR activation, cyber recovery, ransomware response and breach notification

NDIA DR procedures must integrate with security incident, cyber recovery, ransomware, crisis and privacy breach processes so that activation, containment, restoration, forensic preservation, legal and external reporting assessment, stakeholder escalation and post-incident review are coordinated and evidenced.

The NDIA must connect disaster recovery procedures with security incident, ransomware, crisis and privacy breach processes.
